newsitem.title: ITALY: Montedison, Compart see good group, parent H1 net.
newsitem.headline: Montedison, Compart see good group, parent H1 net.

text.p: Italy's agro-industry and chemical conglomerate Montedison SpA and its largest shareholder, Compart, expect a "significant" first half 1996 net profit at both group and parent company level, a Montedison statement said.
Montedison said net debt had fallen further in the first six months and at the start of the second half tax credits of over 500 billion lire had been received.
The Montedison group's gross operating margin in the first half was close to 14 percent of net revenues and that of the Compart group was slightly lower, the statement said.
Compart, the former Ferruzzi Finanziaria holding company, holds some 33 percent of Montedison.
The boards of Compart and Montedison will meet on September 25 to examine first half results.
Montedison managing director Enrico Bondi said in June that full year 1996 results would be broadly in line with those of 1995.
Montedison returned to profit in 1995 with a net consolidated profit of 1.07 trillion lire after a loss of 345 billion lire in 1994.
In the first quarter of 1996 it had a gross operating profit of 786 billion lire, although this was down 16.5 percent from the first quarter of 1995.

But due to a vigorous reorganization plan, Bondi said in June, it was possible that the final 1996 results, despite the fall in first quarter gross operating profit, would not be substantially different from that of 1995.
Today's Montedison statement said current share prices did not reflect the group's economic and financial results.
Montedison closed in Milan on Thursday up 0.03 percent at 929.4 lire, while Compart ended down 1.61 percent at 501.3.

The Montedison statement said no capital operations involving Compart or Montedison were envisaged. Recently, market rumors have resurfaced about a possible merger between Compart and Montedison. Montedison has always denied such talk.
